memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. AB InBev (ABI-BE) at Triaging, 28-Sep-26. The case is a deleveraging compounder in a mature category, sound, middling and fairly priced: the modal total return on the record's path is about 11.3 percent a year over eighteen months and 10.4 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar, a D on the 'Modal return' anchors, so the case parks on the return, not on any gate. The gate line does not bite: no D or F on management ('No mediocre management' B), business quality ('Business' B), predictability ('Transmission' B) or trackability ('Leading indicators' B). Entry level at which the modal path clears the bar: about 68.7 USD on FactSet's basis, about 60 EUR at the 24-Sep-26 cross rate (the record's calculation at that rate, not a currency forecast), roughly 11 percent below the 68.3 EUR price and just below the 200-day average. Two dated triggers reopen the case at a higher price: China volumes flat or better and US depletions above +1 percent at the 3Q26 results on 29-Oct-26; or a lift of the 4 to 8 percent organic EBITDA growth framework at the full-year call in February 2027. Conviction is medium because the earnings arithmetic is firm and the multiple is not.
case: The thesis, as the record states it: AB InBev is a deleveraging compounder in a mature category, not a recovery and not a demand inflection; at 68.3 EUR the shares already pay the stock's own five-year median multiple for the mechanical part of that compounding, so the modal return is about 11 percent a year against the 20 percent bar; the case is sound, middling and fairly priced.

The change is internal, mature and financial in origin. Net debt to normalised EBITDA fell from 3.96x at FY21 to 2.87x at FY25 and 2.86x at 30-Jun-26; net debt fell 15.3 billion USD between FY21 and FY25; 6 billion USD of bonds were redeemed in FY25; Moody's upgraded from A3 to A2 in 2026. The cash that went to creditors now goes to a 6 billion USD buyback (approved 29-Oct-25, 1.9 billion USD done by 24-Jul-26) and a dividend raised 15 percent to 1.15 EUR under a progressive policy. The strategic pivot from mergers to organic category growth on three pillars (category growth, digitisation, optimisation) dates from 2021; the buyback is the one internal force new in the last twelve months; guidance has not been raised in five years. 'Internal forces' is B: shareholder returns A (the programme four times Heineken's 1.5 billion EUR two-year programme); balance sheet B; price rises B (revenue per hectolitre +4.4 percent FY2025, +4.5 percent 1Q26, +4.2 to +4.6 percent 2Q26, with megabrands at 57 percent of revenue contributing 1.0 to 1.5 points of mix); new products B (Beyond Beer +44 percent, no-alcohol +27 percent in 2Q26; BeatBox bought for 493 million USD; non-beer only about 9 percent of the group, its volumes down 1.5 percent in H1-26); standards B (BEES at 72 percent of revenue digital, about 75 percent of orders machine-generated, innovation cycles cut from two years to 100 days); the H1-26 free cash flow step-up B (partly seasonal, not extrapolated). Neutral at C: no chief-executive change, orderly leadership changes, a five-year-old strategy, guidance held, small perimeter moves, small disciplined acquisitions (the 49.9 percent packaging minority bought back for 2.9 billion USD on 30-Jan-26, a reversal of a 2021 sale at about the same price), no new geographies.

The external forces net to a headwind on volume, and the headwind binds because it caps the revenue line the internal forces need. 'External forces' is D. Demand D: global beer volumes 5 percent below 2019, the company's own 1 percent below; US off-trade beer volumes down 5.3 percent over twelve weeks to June 2026, US scanner volumes minus 6 percent in July 2026, alcohol penetration falling across all US income cohorts; China volumes minus 9.7 percent and China EBITDA minus 16.1 percent in 2Q26 as consumers migrate from on-premise nightlife to in-home and online-to-offline channels, a structural shift the risks research named as the single most critical risk before the print; the one tailwind is Latin America, Brazil beer volumes +5.0 percent with revenue per hectolitre +5.3 percent, Colombia low-teens volume growth, record volumes in Mexico and Colombia, and it is regional; moderation, GLP-1 and the World Health Organization's "no safe level" push, with no-alcohol (growing at a 7 percent compound rate to 2028, the company leading) the tailwind inside the headwind. Political and regulatory D: excise tightening (Vietnam's roadmap from 65 percent in 2026 to 90 or 100 percent by 2030, the company at 1 percent share), marketing and packaging rules, Brazilian tax disputes above 53 billion BRL unprovisioned, a Peru excise worst case of 0.6 billion USD; US tariffs on Mexican imports a contingent tailwind. Competition C: tightening in China (Bud China value minus 4 percent in June 2026 against China Resources +6 percent and Yanjing +15 percent; Heineken's licensed China volume up close to 30 percent in 1H26) and Brazil (Heineken's capacity; Ambev +200 basis points of share since 2019, +150 in 1Q26), easing in the US mainstream (Constellation leading with +70 basis points; the company the most aggressive on price and discounting); share gained or held in about 75 percent of markets. Supply C: aluminium the pain point (US hedged can costs up 41 percent; spot near 3,300 USD a tonne against a 3,500 USD threshold), barley benign (about 570 EUR a tonne), transactional hedges turning from headwind to tailwind in H2-26 (Colombia about 12 percent, Brazil about 10 percent), packaging about 45 percent of cost of sales with concentrated suppliers, hedges 12 to 18 months. Macro C: translation unhedged and currently favourable (H1-26 reported +11.5 percent against +5.7 percent organic; a 10 percent stronger dollar takes 91 million USD off pre-tax profit; translation cost 28 US cents of earnings per share over 2023 to 2025; Bolivia's 70 percent devaluation cuts Latin America South EBITDA 10 to 15 percent). Own cycle C: turned in 2026 from destocking to modest volume growth (+0.8 percent 1Q26, +0.9 percent 2Q26), low-amplitude and regional; US depletions +0.3 percent in 1Q26 (only the second positive quarter in thirteen years), minus 1.9 percent in 2Q26; organic revenue has grown every quarter since 1Q22. Disruption C: ready-to-drink and THC take the occasion; BEES (30 markets, 15.0 billion USD quarterly gross merchandise value, a 1.2 billion USD marketplace +50 percent) disrupts the wholesale tier, its profit undisclosed. The World Cup did not lift US volumes (the beer complex minus 3.3 percent in value in the four weeks to 11-Jul-26).
counter_case: The record carries the bull case at the head of the 'Investment Case' as the strongest opposing argument, because it is the one that would change the recommendation. AB InBev is an under-appreciated compounder: a 7 percent free cash flow yield, a 6 billion USD buyback, a path to 2.0x leverage, a digital platform no peer has matched and consistent delivery (consensus met or beaten in 15 of 17 quarters, organic EBITDA inside or above 4 to 8 percent every year since 2021) justify the multiple of a blue-chip consumer staple, and the framework's mediocrity arithmetic is mis-scoring it, since the Cs are the marks of a large, diversified, mature business and not of a weak one. Jefferies puts the stock at 17x against blue-chip peers at 20x one-year-forward; Morgan Stanley at 18.7x, a 10 percent premium to European staples. The sell-side's median target of 94.56 USD is 23 percent above the price; with a 2 percent yield that delivers the bar within eighteen months. The evidence: the 2Q26 print beat on every line, earnings per share +23.4 percent, free cash flow +2.5 billion USD; twelve months of upward revisions; 13 of 17 brokers at Buy; a stock that outperformed distillers and brewers alike for a year. The record concedes that the Cs are of that kind, that the earnings leg is more robust than that of most B cases in the universe, that the stock's own ten-year median (15.8x) and 75th percentile (17.3x) are above where it trades, that the H2-26 margin is probably under-modelled, and that if the multiple reaches 17.3x within eighteen months the return is 22.2 percent a year, a B. It holds its view because the re-rating branch needs two near-independent conditions whose product is about 30 percent; because the cohort peers trade at 11.6 to 11.8x at the bottom of their histories, so the company would be re-rating against a de-rating sector; because the price has already given back 10 percent from the July high through a beat, which is what a market that has paid for the deleveraging and is waiting for volume looks like; because 4 percent revenue growth and 30 basis points of margin a year is not the profile the market pays 17x for in a category whose volumes are 5 percent below 2019; and because the framework rates against a 20 percent bar and a universe, not a sector, so the mediocrity count is the same fact as the D on the return seen from the attributes.

The bear case, carried at the head of the 'Investment Thesis' and taken less seriously for the recommendation: the earnings growth is a "false friend". The margin expansion, cash step-up and beats are what a mature-market brewer produces when it prices above elasticity and under-invests in its brands; volumes sit 1 percent below 2019, US mainstream brands fall 8 to 13 percent a year (Bud Light minus 12.6 percent, Natural Light minus 9.7, Budweiser minus 8.5 in late June 2026), Bud China's value growth is the weakest of the national brewers, the multiple is at par with European staples; the growth is financial engineering on a shrinking volume base, and 2Q26 (North America EBITDA +0.5 percent because top-line gains were fully reinvested, EMEA margin minus 49 basis points, APAC EBITDA minus 10.9 percent) is the first evidence that the reinvestment bill has arrived. The record concedes that the volume base is not growing outside Latin America, that half the earnings growth is below EBIT, and that the premium to Heineken and Carlsberg leaves no margin of safety against the sector. It holds C rather than D because the bear reading's own hard inconsistency is all-time-high Latin American volumes, and Latin America is about 45 percent of revenue and the majority of profit; because pricing sticks at 4 to 5 percent a year with group volumes positive for two quarters; and because the interest and buyback legs are arithmetic. The bear case does not break the earnings path; it caps the multiple, and that cap is already in the modal path.
triggers: - Reopening triggers at a higher price: China volumes flat or better and US depletions above +1 percent at the 3Q26 results on 29-Oct-26; or a lift of the 4 to 8 percent framework at the February 2027 full-year call.
- Entry level on the modal path: about 68.7 USD on FactSet's basis, about 60 EUR at the 24-Sep-26 cross rate, roughly 11 percent below the price.

- The re-rating branch's two conditions: the leverage path on course toward 2.0x (about 2.1x by end-2028 on the record's arithmetic; alarm above 2.8x after the summer cash); the volume base seen to stabilise (China flat or better by mid-2027, US depletions at or above zero).
- The de-rating branch's condition: a cut of 5 percent or more to FY2027 consensus earnings from China or the US consumer.

- The drop-through ratio, in both directions: net interest (4,162 USDm in FY2025; about 3,750 USDm by FY2028 on the record's path; refinancing on the 40 percent of debt in euros), the tax rate against the guided 26 to 28 percent, minorities after the packaging buy-in, the buyback pace and any successor programme after October 2027, any re-leveraging African transaction (alarm a transaction above 5 billion USD; invalidate leverage above 3.0x).

- China: the earnings review's thresholds, flat or better against worse than minus 8 percent at 3Q26; the Bud APAC margin down 300 basis points for two quarters as invalidation; Bud China value share loss for four quarters as invalidation of the channel-migration risk; consensus Asia Pacific revenue growth of about 2.6 percent a year assumes a recovery the point-of-sale data do not show.
